messages:
Maria Liu: quick sync — pushed the jitter/holdtime sweep to canary (3 nodes, 2x A100). collecting 30m of load from prod-replay. initial observation: tail latency improved for p95 when jitter increased to 12-15% but p50 moved up a bit. :thinking:
Devin Park: can you paste the config you ran? curious about coalesce_delay vs hold_time breakdown
Maria Liu: sure — used staged knobs: hold_time_ms=6, coalesce_delay_ms=1.2, jitter_pct=12 (applied as random +/-). token_budget_target=48 for small models, 128 for med.
Samir Gupta: perf-bot flagged a kernel change earlier today — any chance that's confounding?
perf-bot: deployment "runtime-kernel-v2.14" rolled at 3450009000 to canary nodes. no regressions on unit tests but perf tests only run on 256-seqlen workload.
Maria Liu: thanks, noted. I profiled a 512-seqlen chat workload and saw a kernel switch at about 120ms into generation where we flip to fallback matmul path. that aligns with a tiny latency bump in the 2nd token window.
Kevin O'Neil: fallback flip is probably from quant-kernel incompat on new kernel. we saw heuristics prefer the fused-attn up to 64 tokens then fall back.
Devin Park: how does KV cache hit behavior look across micro-batches? any priming thrash?
Maria Liu: KV hits are ~93% for long-lived sessions but drop to 70% in the first 3 tokens when we applied larger coalesce delays. seems micro-batch reordering is priming stale KV shards.
Samir Gupta: can you share a short snippet of the sweep yaml? want to reproduce locally quickly.
Maria Liu: pasted below:
```
microbatch:
  hold_time_ms: 6
  coalesce_delay_ms: 1.2
  jitter_pct: 12
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
queue_policy: priority-ttl
token_budget_target:
  small: 48
  medium: 128
  large: 512
```
Devin Park: neat. if KV priming drops with higher coalesce_delay we should try asymmetric jitter (more jitter on start-of-session requests) so priming doesn't get grouped into later batches.
Kevin O'Neil: +1. Also try biasing kernel selection by sequence-length histogram at routing time — avoid kernels that will flip mid-window if predicted continuation > 60 tokens.
Maria Liu: did a quick canary where jitter_pct=6 but we add start_session_bias=true (reduces coalesce_delay for first batch). p95 tail improved +7% vs baseline, p50 stable. KV hit recovered to ~90% during warmup.
Samir Gupta: any regressions on throughput? throughput dropped ~3%?
Maria Liu: yep small throughput dip, but unit cost per token decreased slightly due to fewer fallbacks. tradeoff seems reasonable for interactive SLOs.
Devin Park: action items?
Maria Liu: 1) run a dedicated kernel-compat check matrix on variable seq lengths (32/128/512) — Kevin to own. 2) add asymmetric jitter flag and start_session_bias rollout in the runtime — Samir to implement. 3) expand perf-bot workloads to include 512-seqlen replay — Devin + perf-bot. 4) hold time tuning: try 4ms/6ms/8ms and compare p50/p95 and kv-hit curves — I'll run overnight.
Kevin O'Neil: I'll add kernel matrix and ping when done. expected finish EOD GMT.
Samir Gupta: starting on asymmetric jitter PR, will put draft later today.
perf-bot: created task PERF-9876: add 512-seqlen job to nightly matrix.
Maria Liu: thanks team. if we see kernel fallback still happening after kernel matrix fixes, we may need to bias routing to the quant-safe variant for canary svc. will post results in this thread tomorrow. :thumbsup:
